page: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Gen9 processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The underlying CPU model is the AWS Neoverse-V3, utilizing the ARMv9 instruction set. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, provides 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench evaluations, as well as in software compilation with Clang. In data processing tasks, it demonstrates top-tier performance for gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations, which reached 136.88 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also in the top tier at 103.35 GB/sec. However, single-core stress-ng CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth read/write operations fall into the average category. Large-model LLM inference is unsupported due to the lack of GPU acceleration, though small-model prompt processing performs in the top tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.12xlarge offers a high density of dedicated physical cores relative to its memory footprint, making it a resource-efficient option for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory allocations. The absence of local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, which represents an architectural tradeoff. This instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded data decompression.
